absent: Full memory ordering and lifetime guarantees for RCU protected traversal and publication beyond observed pairing of read sections with pointer operations.
Complete layouts and valid flag combinations for array, cursor, node and configuration structures beyond fields touched by routed fragments.
Exact allocation, scheduling and interrupt contexts allowed for each operation beyond observed lock pairing and retry placement.
Detailed algorithm behavior for individual text search implementations and generic find iteration beyond linear adaptation.
Full timer queue lifecycle including initialization, head layout and concurrency requirements beyond insertion and removal ordering.
Precise destruction and shrink reclamation rules for multi-level trees beyond observed empty and single entry cases.
Error marker encoding and propagation details beyond observed invalid, memory, exists and not-found outcomes.

findings.text: Array range store accepts a target array plus inclusive bounds and a uniform entry with an allocation mask, and reports a result marker covering success or failure. A null entry acts as removal over the span, while non-null entries are materialized across the interval with allocation retry handled internally.

Split preparation and split execution are exposed as companion operations that narrow a wide ordered entry into smaller entries or child nodes. Preparation builds reserved structures in advance, while execution publishes them, with a best-effort variant that may allocate late under restrictive context.

Text search exposes registration and unregistration for named algorithms, preparation and destruction for pattern configurations, and a continuous buffer search helper. Preparation binds a configuration to its algorithm operations, while destruction releases algorithm resources and the configuration itself.
Timer queue exposes insertion and removal over a cached ordered tree keyed by expiry. Insertion signals whether the new element becomes earliest, while removal signals whether elements remain.
Node deletion helper removes a whole tree node through a transient cursor positioned from the node location metadata, delegating accounting updates to a caller supplied callback.

Range store rejects special internal values and inverted bounds with an invalid argument marker, without mutating the array. Successful stores cover the entire requested span by advancing in operation sized steps until the end is passed.
Range sizing selects a shift and sibling span that remain inside the requested bounds and respect chunk alignment, preferring the widest aligned coverage that does not overshoot the end.
Splitting preserves per-mark presence from the original slot onto each replacement slot or child, and maintains value accounting so nodes track how many entries hold values versus pointers.

Split reservation honors the array accounting flag by propagating it into the allocation mask, chains reserved nodes through parent linkage, and on failure releases state and records a memory shortage.

Algorithm registration requires a name plus core callbacks for lookup, initialization and pattern introspection, rejects duplicates and incomplete definitions, and maintains a globally visible list for later lookup.

Preparation rejects empty patterns, resolves the named algorithm with optional on-demand loading, delegates configuration creation to the algorithm initializer, and links the resulting configuration back to its operations with failure signaled by error markers.
Linear search adaptation presents a single contiguous buffer as successive blocks by returning the unconsumed tail from the current offset and reporting exhaustion once fully consumed.
Queue order is defined solely by expiry comparison, with the cached structure always able to report the earliest element efficiently.

Self tests exercise range stores around small and page sized boundaries, ordered splits across chunk levels, allocation alignment, working set tracking, order queries including conflict iteration, and destruction of empty and populated arrays, with an empty no-op variant for unsupported configurations.

Range mutation and working set updates acquire the cursor lock for the mutating section and release before allocation retry, so retries occur outside the critical section. Split execution and in-place slot filling are performed while the caller holds the cursor lock.

Registry mutation uses a dedicated spin lock held across duplicate checks and list updates, while algorithm lookup uses a read side critical section that safely walks the list and acquires a module reference on match.
Linear state carries a length plus a pointer to contiguous data, stored inside the generic search state control block and interpreted by the block provider.

Observed tree nodes carry a back pointer to the owning array, a slot table, parent linkage, level and position metadata, occupancy and value tallies, and list linkage for shadow tracking. Observed cursors carry index, shift, sibling span, node and offset position, allocation chain, least-recently-used hint and update callback.

Cursor operations follow an attempt, release and retry cycle where allocation shortage is reported through cursor state, resources are released outside the lock, and the whole attempt repeats until success or a non-retryable outcome.

Ordered split follows reservation then publication, where reserved nodes are chained privately, consumed one by one during vertical expansion, and any leftover chain remains for cleanup, with marks and tallies updated as publication proceeds.

Shadow membership toggles with node content, joining the global shadow list when occupancy indicates all values and leaving otherwise, with a drain phase that repeatedly removes the first member and deletes its node under array lock until empty.

Self-test driver runs a broad suite of array checks in sequence and logs overall pass tallies, returning an invalid marker unless every check passes, with a companion exit routine that performs no action.
Focused test entries validate accounting tallies, order retrieval through array and cursor paths, conflict iteration order reporting, and destruction semantics for empty and populated instances.
Splitting entries whose order far exceeds the current cursor level is unsupported and handled as allocation failure after warning, requiring callers to avoid such wide splits.

Best-effort split cannot handle sibling fan-out combined with vertical expansion nor cascades needing multiple new nodes, and reports an invalid argument outcome for those shapes instead of partial mutation.
Inserting an already queued element or removing an element that is not queued triggers a one-time warning, indicating caller tracking errors around queue membership.

Registering incomplete algorithm definitions or duplicate names, unregistering unknown entries, and preparing unknown algorithms or empty patterns all fail cleanly with error markers rather than corrupting the registry.

Observed error signaling uses invalid argument for bad ranges, internal values and unsupported split shapes, memory shortage for allocation failures, already-exists for duplicate algorithm names, and not-found for unknown algorithms or missing unregister targets.
Chunk geometry and mark iteration bounds govern sizing and mark propagation, with order derived from trailing alignment of the inclusive end and sibling masks derived from order modulo chunk width.
Accounting propagation, restrictive late allocation context, bounded allocation limits and optional autoload control allocation and lookup behavior without changing core semantics.
